RedAlert2.title: RedAlert2
RedAlert2.engine:
Westwood 2D DirectDraw engine, always 16 bpp.
- Red Alert 2 1.006: game.exe, md5 282f160e...
- Yuri's Revenge 1.001: gamemd.exe, md5 03452ffd...
- Both start through the Ra2.exe / RA2MD.exe stubs.
- gamemd.exe differs from gamemd.old in 14 byte runs (re-counted with cmp). None is in the list builders, the options constructor or loader, or the mode enumerator.
- The game-local aqrit ddraw.dll (27,136 B, PE subsystem 4.0) is a pass-through proxy. It re-exports the DirectDraw entry points and has no EnumDisplayModes code.
- aqrit.cfg sets ForceDirectDrawEmulation=1 on XP. On Vista+ the launcher copies in _win7\aqrit.cfg, which sets it to 0.
RedAlert2.launch_sets:
Gameplay runs at 1920x1080x16 on all four LCD boxes.
- Mechanism: both launchers CALL FLEETRES.BAT, then run FLEETRES.EXE -ini RA2.INI / RA2MD.INI Video ScreenWidth %FR_W% and ScreenHeight %FR_H%. This is WritePrivateProfileString, so other keys survive. gameres.h:743-746 write the same values at sync.
- The deployed ra2.ini is byte-identical on .123, .145 and .240 (md5 8d9f9fec...): ScreenWidth=1920, ScreenHeight=1080, and no AllowHiResModes.
- Measured today: while RA2 ran, DISPLAYCFG get read 1920x1080 at 16 bpp on both .145 and .240.
- The main shell is a fixed 800x600 surface centred at (560,240). That is expected.
- The prior agent's .240 caveat (no EDID, next launch falls back to 1024x768) is stale. GAMERES on .240 at 00:40 reports EDID DELL E2313H, persisted and live desktop 1920x1080, and a wide target of 1920x1080.
RedAlert2.menu_source:
The list comes from the driver, filtered in code. Confirmed on hardware.
- Path: main menu -> Options (dialog 213) -> 'Set Game Resolution' drop-down (ctrl 1773).
- Fill: IDirectDraw::EnumDisplayModes (flags 0) through the helper at 0x4962a0. A mode is kept only if dwRGBBitCount (desc+0x54) is 16 and 640x480 <= mode <= max. Entries are labelled '%d x %d x 16'.
- Filter: with [Video] AllowHiResModes=yes the max is 4096x4096. Otherwise the max is 1024x768 and only widths 640, 800 and 1024 pass.
- The constructor at 0x5d8840 sets the flag to 0. Only the loader at 0x5d8de0 reads it (the sole xref to the string), so the game never writes it. Neither staged ini carries it.
- Seen on .145 today: the drop-down listed exactly 640x480x16, 800x600x16 and 1024x768x16. Its current-value box was blank, because the running 1920x1080 mode is filtered out.
- DirectDraw on that same box does enumerate 1920x1080x16.

RedAlert2.fix:
Correct as proposed, and now hardware-verified on .145 with a temporary ini (the RA2 test above).

Library change:
1. Add AllowHiResModes=yes under [Video] in the staged ra2.ini and RA2MD.INI.
2. Add launcher lines "%~dp0FLEETRES.EXE" -ini "%~dp0RA2.INI" Video AllowHiResModes yes, and the same for RA2MD.INI. They must go in as a stage-fleetres.py 'fix' repair pair: patch_launcher() returns early when the launcher already contains the FLEETRES call (MARK), as both launchers do.
3. Add gameres.h rows {RedAlert2, GR_OP_INI, RA2.INI/RA2MD.INI, Video, AllowHiResModes, yes}.
4. Add a staging test that pins those lines. test_gameres_mirror only checks file names.
5. Correct the RedAlert2 recipe comment at stage-fleetres.py:1108-1110. It says the aqrit wrapper 'lets the Westwood engine take a mode its own menu never offers'. In fact the engine reads ScreenWidth/ScreenHeight from the ini itself, and the wrapper has no mode code.
6. Record the menu fact in PER-TITLE-STATUS.md.
7. Then purge and GAMESYNC RedAlert2 on every box, per the staged-game loop.

The staged ini alone would be enough, because the game keeps the key. Steps 2-3 follow the Tiberian Sun precedent as a safeguard.
RedAlert2.fix_source: Already in the tree. AllowHiResModes is a stock engine key, read by game.exe at 0x5d8de0 and gamemd.exe at 0x5fa943. Nothing needs downloading. Do not mix in the legacy cnc-ddraw stack at Utility/Retro Automation/ra2-opt.
RedAlert2.fix_risk:
Low.
- The flag only widens the Options list and is read nowhere else.
- Westwood's INI writer keeps a key it reads but never writes. Observed today on Tiberian Sun: the game rewrote SUN.INI, adding [Intro] PlaySide00/01, and AllowHiResModes=yes and VideoBackBuffer survived (EVR/240_SUN.INI.before and .after). RA2 uses the same INIClass.
- An in-game mode pick lasts until the next launch, because the launcher rewrites ScreenWidth/ScreenHeight. GAMERES also rewrites them at sync.
- The launcher and GAMERES would both write 'yes', so they cannot fight.
- LAN is unaffected. Resolution is local to each client, and WOLLimitResolution applies only to Westwood Online. Mixed 1080p and 1024x768 peers already play two-box.
- On a CRT box the list simply shows that driver's 16-bpp modes.

StarCraft.title: StarCraft
StarCraft.engine:
Blizzard Storm/DirectDraw 8-bit 2D engine, StarCraft and Brood War 1.16.1.
- StarCraft.exe (md5 50d53a3b...) is identical in the root and in BroodWar\.
- storm.dll (md5 76a285e2...) is identical in both too.
- Each game mounts its own disc image from _disc\ with Daemon Tools.
StarCraft.launch_sets:
Always 640x480x8 exclusive DirectDraw.
- StarCraft.exe asks for SetDisplayMode(640,480,8) at 0x41da48.
- Only if that fails does it fall back, at 0x41da6c, to SetDisplayMode(GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXSCREEN), GetSystemMetrics(SM_CYSCREEN), 8): the desktop size at 8 bpp. This is not user-selectable.
- Neither launcher has FLEETRES, and none applies.
- How a 640x480 mode appears on the 16:9 panel (stretched or pillarboxed) depends on the GPU and monitor scaler. It is UNKNOWN: GDI only ever sees the 640x480 surface, and nobody has looked at the screens.

CHANGED from the prior answer: .123 is no longer excluded.
- HWPROFILE on .123 reports disc_mount=true (evidence 'd347bus', Daemon Tools 3.47; daemon.exe is running).
- .123's All Users desktop carries StarCraft.lnk and 'StarCraft - Brood War.lnk', written by tonight's GAMESYNC at 2026-09-29 03:47 UTC.
- Whether StarCraft actually runs on .123 is untested.
StarCraft.menu_source:
There is no resolution option.
- The only requested mode is the immediate 640x480x8, plus the desktop-size fallback that fires only on failure.
- The storm.dll display init is called with 640x480 (0x41d528).
- install.reg and FLEET-NOTES.txt confirm there is no windowed mode. The only switches in the binary are ddemulate and nosound.
StarCraft.evidence:
Static (re-disassembled independently):
- StarCraft.exe 0x41da3b: push 8; push 0x1e0; push 0x280; call [ecx+0x54].
- On failure, 0x41da4f loads GetSystemMetrics (IAT 0x4fe368). Then: push 0 -> SM_CXSCREEN, push 1 -> SM_CYSCREEN, push 8, call [edx+0x54] at 0x41da6c.
- The prior agent searched only for the byte pattern 'ff 51 54', so it missed this 'ff 52 54' site.

Mounter and shortcuts on .123:

- The Resolution Expander injector is not on the share.

WarcraftOrcsAndHumans.title: WarcraftOrcsAndHumans
WarcraftOrcsAndHumans.engine:
DOS WAR.EXE (DOS4GW LE, GOG 1.2) in VGA mode 13h (320x200x256).
- Re-checked: exactly one 'mov eax,13h; int 10h' at file offset 0x3474f, and no VESA 4F02h anywhere.
- Runs under GOG's DOSBox 0.74-2.1 (DOSBox.exe md5 2318a446..., SDL.dll md5 b8b92fee...). Daggerfall and MOO2 ship the same build.
- That build offers the surface, overlay, opengl, openglnb and ddraw outputs.
WarcraftOrcsAndHumans.launch_sets:
The defect is real and was reproduced on hardware today.
- With the deployed conf (output=surface, fullresolution=desktop), WC1 shows an unscaled 640x480 frame at (640,300)-(1280,780) of the 1920x1080 panel.
- Seen on .145 (XP) and .195 (Win7): EVR/wc1_145_A_deployed_surface.png and wc1_195_A_deployed_surface.png.
- Cause: DOSBox's surface output cannot scale. Its own help text says 'try an output different from surface' and 'output=surface does not!' [support hardware scaling].
- The launchers (FLEETRES -ini dosboxWC1.conf sdl fullresolution %FR_DOSFULLRES%) and GAMERES (gameres.h:799) handle fullresolution correctly.
- The .240 caveat (no EDID, so 'original') is stale. GAMERES on .240 now reports dosbox_fullresolution=desktop.

Postal.title: Postal
Postal.engine:
Running With Scissors' SDL2 rebuild, 'POSTAL Classic and Uncut' (GOG).
- Postal.exe md5 986a6395..., PE subsystem 5.1, imports only KERNEL32 and SDL2.
- It needs SSE2. All four LCD boxes have it (Athlon 64 on .123 and .240, i5-2400 on .145 and .195, per docs/fleet-inventory.md).
- It renders an 8-bit frame, converted into an ARGB8888 streaming texture (SDL_CreateTexture format 0x16362004) through SDL_Renderer.
Postal.launch_sets:
Hardware-verified on .240. This was the title's first launch on any box.
- The 'Postal' SDL_app window is at 0,0-1920x1080 and in the foreground.
- The desktop mode stays at 1920x1080x32, so this is fullscreen-desktop with no mode switch, as the binary predicts.

CORRECTION to the prior agent:
- The title screen, main menu and options screens are 640x480 art pillarboxed to 1440x1080 in the centre of the panel (content x=239..1679), with black bars about 240 px on each side. They do not fill the panel.
- The game's UI code centres 640-wide elements with (w-640)/2 (e.g. at 0x42b61b). Only the gameplay view uses the full 853x480 logical frame, and gameplay was not observed.

The size follows the LIVE desktop (SDL_GetDesktopDisplayMode):
- All four LCD boxes have a persisted desktop of 1920x1080 today (GAMERES).
- docs/fleet-inventory.md still says 1024x768 for .145, which is stale.
- The launcher CALLs FLEETRES.BAT but writes nothing, which is correct.
Postal.menu_source:
There is no resolution option. Confirmed on hardware.
- Main menu: START / OPTIONS / EXIT.
- OPTIONS: AUDIO, CONTROLS, PERFORMANCE, DIFFICULTY and GAME. There is NO 'VIDEO' entry here, which corrects the prior agent's 'OPTIONS -> VIDEO -> GAMMA'.
- PERFORMANCE: TRANSPARENCY, 3D LIGHTING, PARTICLES, DYNAMIC VOLUME, AMBIENT SOUNDS.
- GAME: COAT COLOR, CROSSHAIR.
- The VIDEO/GAMMA strings do exist in the exe, probably in the in-game Esc menu (not observed).
- The only size control is the '-resolution WxH' command line, which makes a real SDL_WINDOW_FULLSCREEN window of that size. The internal frame stays (desktop_w*480/desktop_h) x 480.
- rspSetVideoMode (0x42fc50) never reads its depth, device-width or device-height arguments, so POSTAL.INI's DeviceWidth, DeviceHeight and UseCurrentDeviceDimensions have no effect on the window.

Carmageddon2.title: Carmageddon2
Carmageddon2.engine: BRender Win32, CARMA2_HW.EXE v1.02a, Glide renderer (install.reg Driver=2, box-246 A/B: Driver=3 Direct3D crashes) through the game-local nGlide 1.02 (glide2x/glide3x/glide.dll, glide2x.dll md5 e4867e04, which wraps Glide to Direct3D 9)
Carmageddon2.launch_sets: Confirmed and measured. Play Carmageddon 2.bat calls FLEETRES.BAT only for FR_GLIDE (the glide_swap block) and writes no resolution. gameres.h has no rule for this title. HKCU\Software\Zeus Software is absent on all four LCD boxes (REGREAD re-checked tonight; the same REGREAD with a spaced path works on HKCU Control Panel\Desktop), so nGlide runs 'By app'. MEASURED on .123 (XP, HD 3850): with the staged launcher, DISPLAYCFG went to 640x480x32, the Carma2MainWndClass window was 0,0-640x480, and the front end was captured as a 640x480 frame. The monitor's scaler then stretches that to the panel.
Carmageddon2.menu_source: No in-game resolution setting. Graphics data exist only for 320x200 and 640x480 (data\32X20X8, data\64x48x8; '640x480 init string', 'Screen width/height doesn't match graf data'). The complete switch list is -SCALEMOUSE -AFE -ALIEN -BLOOD -ZOMBIE -D3D -NOCUTSCENES -NOCUTSCENE; the survey omitted -D3D. The only resolution chooser is the external nglide_config.exe. Its table, independently confirmed from glide2x.dll's own code, is index 0 By app, 1 By desktop, 2 640x480, 3 800x600, 5 1024x768, 6 1152x864, 10 1280x960, 11 1280x1024, 19 1600x1200, 21 1920x1080, clamped below 29. Aspect is 0 Fit to screen or 1 4:3.
Carmageddon2.evidence: glide2x.dll disassembly (capstone): RegOpenKeyExA(0x80000001 HKCU, 'Software\Zeus Software\nGlide') at VA 0x100025dc. 'Resolution', 'Aspect', 'Refresh', 'Vsync', 'Gamma' and 'Splash' are each read with an untyped RegQueryValueExA into a 255-byte buffer, then sscanf('%d'); Resolution is clamped to < 0x1d. The width/height table is built on the stack, with index 21 = 0x780 x 0x438. DllMain PROCESS_ATTACH stores GetSystemMetrics(0/1), the live desktop size, at VA 0x10001661. Hardware (.123), under .claude/evidence-1080p/review-dosbox-descent-carma/hw/: baseline 123_carma2_baseline_25s.png (640x480); with the values 123_carma2_nglide_bydesktop_15s.png and 123_carma2_nglide_bydesktop_27s.png (FMV inside x=240..1680) and 123_carma2_after_esc3.png (front end at x=240..1680, full height, DISPLAYCFG 1920x1080x32 throughout). Agent log hw/logs/123-agent.log.1.
Carmageddon2.fix: VERIFIED on .123: HKCU\Software\Zeus Software\nGlide with Resolution="1" and Aspect="1", both REG_SZ. DISPLAYCFG stayed 1920x1080 and every frame (FMV and front end) was nGlide-rendered as a correct 4:3 1440x1080 pillarbox at x=240..1680. Implement it in the launcher, before start "" CARMA2_HW.EXE: FLEETRES.EXE -reg HKCU "Software\Zeus Software\nGlide" Resolution sz <idx>, and the same for Aspect with sz 1. Prefer an explicit per-box index over '1 By desktop'. 'By desktop' is the LIVE desktop: GetSystemMetrics is read when glide2x.dll loads, so a desktop another game stranded at 640x480 yields 640x480. That is exactly the failure FLEETRES avoids by reading the persisted mode. Map %FR_W%x%FR_H% in cmd: 1920x1080 -> 21, 1280x960 -> 10, 1152x864 -> 6, 1024x768 -> 5, 800x600 -> 3, anything else -> 1. The values must be REG_SZ: a REG_DWORD reads as raw bytes, sscanf fails, and the default 'By app' silently remains. install.reg alone is weaker, because it is only merged at GAMESYNC.
Carmageddon2.fix_source: Already in the tree: nGlide 1.02 in Carmageddon2\, and FLEETRES.EXE -reg ... sz (fleetres.c writes REG_SZ for any type other than dword). The change goes into the Carmageddon2 entry in scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py (a post/marker block like glide_swap). No download.
Carmageddon2.fix_risk: Low for display and aspect, now measured. Not observed: in-race 3D. The front end ignores synthetic clicks and Enter: a click on START at the 640x480 baseline did nothing (123_carma2_baseline_click2.png). ESC does skip the intro FMVs, which refutes 'ignores keys' for the FMV stage only. The HKCU key is global per user. Only UnrealGold also ships nGlide, and UE1 reaches it only through GlideDrv on GlideRender opt-in boxes, where the launcher moves the wrapper aside. Write the values at every launch: during this test another concurrent session REGDELETEd HKCU\Software\Zeus Software on .123 (agent log [00:43:50] box time) and also taskkilled my CARMA2_HW.EXE ([00:43:03]), so state set once can vanish. Pre-existing and unrelated to 1080p: glide_swap keys off FR_GLIDE (silicon present), not the GlideRender opt-in that FR_UE1DEV uses. On a box like .143, whose Voodoo is a secondary adapter behind the card driving the monitor, the launcher removes nGlide and the game would render to the Voodoo.
Carmageddon2.hw_check: On .123 (done) or .145: write the two REG_SZ values with EXEC cmd /c reg add "HKCU\Software\Zeus Software\nGlide" /v Resolution /t REG_SZ /d 21 /f, and the same for Aspect with /d 1. Then EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Carmageddon2" "Play Carmageddon 2.bat". After 8-15 s DISPLAYCFG must read 1920x1080, not 640x480, and SCREENSHOT 0 should have its bbox at x=240..1680. Send UIKEY ESCAPE twice to reach the front end and SCREENSHOT it. In-race needs a human, because clicks on START are ignored. Then taskkill /f /im "CARMA2_HW.EXE", confirm DISPLAYCFG 1920x1080, and delete the test key with reg delete "HKCU\Software\Zeus Software" /f if the fix is not yet staged.
Carmageddon2.verifier_notes: Survey fix CONFIRMED on hardware, with refinements: use an explicit index rather than By desktop, REG_SZ is mandatory, and write at every launch. Correction: add -D3D (and -NOCUTSCENE) to the switch list. Correction: 'front end ignores click and key' is partly wrong, because ESC skips the FMVs. ShadowWarrior.engine: Build engine (3D Realms), original DOS Shadow Warrior 1.2 (SW.EXE = SW.DAT, md5 0c76df2d; Wanton.dat for Wanton Destruction; each launch runs @COPY SW.DAT/WANTON.DAT sw.exe), GOG's DOSBox 0.74. Not a source port.

The dosboxSW_sw/_td/_wd/_lan and _swipxhost confs are [ipx]/[autoexec] only. GAMERES rule: gameres.h:798. The staged and deployed dosbox_swarrior.conf both have aspect=false at line 52. ShadowWarrior.menu_source: The Options menu has no resolution item. SW.DAT contains '%d x %d mode selected.', the 'swres' cheat, 'VESA mode %ld x %ld not found' and the getvalidvesamodes code, so F5/swres cycle VBE-reported modes: the original 3DR ResChange keeps 320x200, 640x400, 640x480 and 800x600. That comes from the jfsw commented-out source; it was not observed in game. SETUP (Setmain.exe) has a HARDCODED 'Choose a VESA 1.0/2.0 Mode' list of 320x200, 320x400, 640x480, 800x600, confirmed in strings (no formatter). DOSBox 0.74's S3 VBE maximum is 1280x1024, with no 1920x1080.
ShadowWarrior.evidence: Staged tree /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/ShadowWarrior: five launchers, dosbox_swarrior.conf (fullresolution=desktop, output=overlay, machine=svga_s3, aspect=false, scaler=normal2x), SW.CFG ScreenMode=2 320x200 (dragon\SW.CFG identical, md5 ec62e1b5), Setmain.exe strings. Hardware, under .claude/evidence-1080p/review-dosbox-descent-carma/hw/: 195_sw_baseline_25s.png (bbox 96..1824, the defect) and 195_sw_aspecttrue_25s.png (bbox 240..1679 with the fix).
ShadowWarrior.fix: VERIFIED on .195. Passing a conf that contains only '[render]' / 'aspect=true' AFTER the others changed the main menu to 1440x1080 at x=240..1679. That confirms DOSBox 0.74 lets a later -conf override the key. The simplest staged fix is to change aspect=false to aspect=true in dosbox_swarrior.conf, which is right on both LCDs and CRTs (on a CRT with 'original', DOSBox then asks for 640x480 instead of 640x400). Alternatively, append [render] aspect=true to the four dosboxSW_*.conf files. Optional sharper picture, still 4:3 and untested: SW.CFG ScreenMode=1 (VESA 2.0) with 640x480 or 800x600, both on SETUP's list and in DOSBox's VBE table.
ShadowWarrior.fix_source: Already in the tree: one key in Games-Library/ShadowWarrior/dosbox_swarrior.conf (or the four dosboxSW_*.conf). No download. It reaches boxes only through GAMESYNC (GAMESYNC RESET+START on provisioned boxes, because the boot-time sync idles once gamesync.done exists).
ShadowWarrior.fix_risk: Very low. The key is overlay-scaled, so there is no CPU cost, and it is right on every panel type, so it can be a staged constant. No LAN impact. The fix must reach all five launchers; either location covers them.
ShadowWarrior.hw_check: Done on .195. To repeat on XP (.145): EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\ShadowWarrior" "Play Shadow Warrior.bat" and wait about 25 s for the main menu without sending keys. SCREENSHOT should show bbox x=240..1680 after the fix (x=96..1824 today). Kill with taskkill /f /im "DOSBox.exe" or PROCKILL. Descent3.launch_sets: REFUTED in effect. The survey and PER-TITLE-STATUS ('Descent3 1080p') assume -Width/-Height gives a 1920x1080 game. MEASURED: -Width 1920 -Height 1080 does switch the display to 1920x1080 (DISPLAYCFG 1920x1080x16, 'Descent 3' window 0,0-1920x1080), but the in-flight view is a 640x480 box centred on a black screen. This was seen at x=640..1280, y=300..780 on .195 (Win7, HD 5450) and on .240 (XP, X800); the HUD message line at the top is still laid out on the full 1920 width. The same happened with -Width 1280 -Height 960 (a 640x480 box in a 1280x960 mode) and with RS_resolution=5 (list 1280x960) and no switches. Cause, from the source release and confirmed on hardware: at SM_GAME the 3D window is sized from the PILOT file's saved game_window_w/h (InitGameScreen(gw,gh), clamped to the display), unless the resolution was just changed in the Video menu. The staged Descent3\sdf.plt stores 640x480 at file offsets 0x1F/0x23. Pressing '=' about 12 times grows the window to full screen; after that the 4:3 projection is visibly stretched 1.33x on 16:9, because rend_GetAspectRatio assumes a 4:3 monitor. The menus themselves always run at 640x480x16.
Descent3.menu_source: VERIFIED on .195. Options > VIDEO > RESOLUTION shows exactly seven hardcoded 4:3 buttons: 512x384, 640x480, 800x600, 960x720, 1024x768, 1280x960, 1600x1200. None is checked when the game is started with -Width/-Height, because the custom slot has no button (195_d3_options.png). The survey's claim that these menus 'CANNOT be driven by the agent' is REFUTED. On .195 and .240 UIKEY ESCAPE skipped the intro movie, Enter chose the pilot, arrows and Enter walked the main menu into Options and New Game > Pilot Training, and '=' resized the in-game view. README-FLEET.txt and requires.json say otherwise and are out of date.
Descent3.evidence: Under .claude/evidence-1080p/review-dosbox-descent-carma/hw/: 195_d3_options.png (the list); 195_d3_after_training_21s.png and 195_d3_ingame_46s.png (640x480 box inside 1920x1080); 195_d3_1280_ingame.png (box inside 1280x960); 195_d3_rsres5_ingame.png; 240_d3_1080_ingame.png (XP, same box); 240_d3_after_eq12.png ('=' x12: full screen, stretched); 240_d3_rvw_ingame_noaspect.png (patched pilot: full 1920x1080 from level start); 240_d3_rvw_ingame_aspect178.png (patched pilot plus -aspect 1.78); rvw.plt.test-pilot; 240_sdf.plt.after-test and 195_sdf.plt.after-test (the game upgrades the pilot 0x2A->0x2B, 1770->1772 B, at mission start). Source: DescentDevelopers/Descent3 pilot_class.cpp read_hud_data (uint8 hud_mode, uint16 hud_stat, uint16 hud_graphical_stat, int game_window_w, int game_window_h) and game.cpp SetScreenMode(SM_GAME) -> InitGameScreen, which clamps to Max_window_w/h.
Descent3.fix: (1) The real fix: stage Descent3\sdf.plt with its saved game window raised. Assert the old dwords 640/480 at offsets 0x1F/0x23 of the version-0x2A file, then write 4096/4096. InitGameScreen clamps to the display, so this one staged constant is right on every box (1920x1080 on the LCDs, the tube's own mode on CRTs). VERIFIED on .240 with a temporary copy (rvw.plt, -pilot RVW): the level opened full-screen at 1920x1080. Keep -Width %FR_W% -Height %FR_H% in both client launchers. (2) Add -pilot SDF to 'Play Descent 3.bat' (the Join launcher already has it); otherwise every start stops at the PILOTS dialog. (3) Optional: -aspect 1.78 on 16:9 panels (set D3ASP from FR_ASPECT; 1.6 for 16:10). It fixes proportions (the doorframe became about 390x390 from 390x290), with the trade-off in fix_risk. (4) Update PER-TITLE-STATUS, README-FLEET and requires.json: drop the stale disc_mount and the 'not automatable' note. Optionally stage RS_bitdepth=32 in install.reg, since the game runs 16-bit by default. That is cosmetic.
Descent3.fix_source: Already in the tree: a small byte edit to the staged sdf.plt (no generator exists for it; stage-fleetres.py has no binary writer), plus 'Play Descent 3.bat' generated from the stage-fleetres.py 'Descent3' entry. 'Join Descent 3 - LAN.bat' is hand-written (no generator in the repo). -aspect is in main.exe 1.4 and in README.TXT. No download.
Descent3.fix_risk: Pilot patch: low. The offsets are specific to pilot version 0x2A, so the patch must assert 640/480 first. The game rewrites sdf.plt at the first mission start on each box (upgrading it to 0x2B and saving the clamped size), so after play the box's copy differs from the library and GAMESYNC will re-copy it; that is benign. Multiplayer and the dedicated server are unaffected. -aspect 1.78, measured: 1.4 applies it by zooming the vertical axis (the source's 'if (s <= 0.0f)' branch never scales x). The vertical field of view shrinks, the 3D cockpit's radar and weapon monitors are pushed partly off the bottom of the screen, and the 2D shield/energy readouts no longer sit on the cockpit. Without it, the full-screen view is the 4:3 projection stretched 1.33x. That is a taste call; the pilot fix is not.
Descent3.hw_check: On .240 or .195 (no human needed): EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Descent3" "Play Descent 3.bat". Press UIKEY ESCAPE to skip the long intro and UIKEY RETURN at PILOTS (SDF). For the menu check: DOWN x3, RETURN, SCREENSHOT the VIDEO page, then ESC. For the in-game check: UP x3, RETURN (New Game), DOWN, RETURN (Pilot Training), wait about 25 s, then DISPLAYCFG (1920x1080x16) and SCREENSHOT 0. It works on XP and was also captured on Win7 .195. Expect bbox 0..1920 after the fix (x=640..1280 today). Clean up afterwards: taskkill /f /im "main.exe"; delete C:\Games\Descent3\custom\cache\d3s*.tmp and .lock (a killed run leaves about 1.2 MB there); restore sdf.plt from the library with copy /y from \\192.168.1.122\files\Files\Games-Library\Descent3\sdf.plt, which keeps its mtime.
Descent3.verifier_notes: MAJOR correction. The staged launcher has never produced a 1080p game: 1920x1080 display, 640x480 view. The survey's -aspect fix is valid for proportions but secondary and has side effects; the pilot file is the primary fix. menu 'no' is CONFIRMED on hardware, and 'menus not agent-drivable' is REFUTED. The earlier '.240 1920x1080 verified' compat row is a desktop screenshot, as the survey said. Cleanup verified: sdf.plt matches the library on .123, .195 and .240 (restored on .195 and .240 by copy from the share, original mtime); .195's RS_resolution was put back to 7 (the only registry value I changed); the cache temp files were deleted on all three boxes; rvw.plt and _review_d3.bat were deleted. My first .123 run was disrupted by another session's windowed GLQuake, so the results come from .195 and .240. These findings (pilot-window cause, keyboard-drivable menus, Win7 capture works for this DX6-era title) belong in FINDINGS.md and PER-TITLE-STATUS.md in the fix phase.

Quake1.title: Quake1
Quake1.engine: id Quake: GLQUAKE.EXE (id gl_vidnt.c build, md5 bcf4049319feb518b8c915ac1cc8219b, 'Exe: 15:17:32 Nov 7 1997'; the title plate reads '(GL 0.97) 1.09'; VOODOO\GLQUAKE.EXE is byte-identical) on 1.08 data. WINQUAKE.EXE (software, md5 0b62b82dea48408f45369e1fab53eb0c) is a second shortcut.
Quake1.launch_sets: 800x600x32 fullscreen on all four 1080p LCDs, caused by the launcher's own -cap. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-29 00:3x: I ran each box's DEPLOYED C:\Games\Quake1\FLEETRES.EXE -cmd -cap 1280 960. On .123, .145, .195 and .240 alike it returned FR_W/H=1280x720 and FR_W43/H43=800x600, and FR_LIVE/FR_DESK=1920x1080. Play Quake.bat passes GLQUAKE.EXE -width %FR_W43% -height %FR_H43% -bpp 32. fleetres.c 787-799 keeps the panel's 16:9 aspect under the cap (1280x720), and the classic 4:3 ladder under a 720-line target stops at 800x600. PER-TITLE-STATUS ('capped 1280x960') is wrong. The .246 compat note that blames GLQuake's table is also wrong. The compat DB measured 800x600 on .123, .240 and .246/.195. The deployed launcher equals the staged one on all four boxes (md5 b263c4414c). There is no GAMERES rule (command-line title). The Software shortcut passes no mode.
Quake1.menu_source: Options > Video Modes is READ-ONLY. It prints 'Video modes must be set from the command line with -width...' and has no selectable control. The list is driver-enumerated, not a fixed table. VID_InitFullDIB takes EnumDisplaySettings modes with bpp>=15 that pass CDS_TEST, one slot per WxHxBPP, and stops at 30 slots (cmp 0x1e at 0x415881). Slot 0 is the windowed mode, which leaves 29. MEASURED ON .123 (ATI HD 3850, XP): I ran a windowed GLQuake with vid_describemodes in the console and took a screenshot. The ATI driver enumerates RESOLUTION-MAJOR, 16 then 32 bpp per resolution, and the list ends at '29: 1920x1080x16 fullscreen'. 1920x1080x32 does not fit, so the launcher's -bpp 32 can never reach 1080p there, and today's page shows 1920x1080x16 only as text. The order is per driver. .145's measurements (glh2 1920x1080 works at 16 bpp, GLQuake -bpp 32 fails) fit bpp-major. .240's list starts with six sub-640 modes, so if it is resolution-major like .123 it fills at 1280x720x16 (inferred from the 2026-08-31 glh2 failures). With -current, every entry reads 'Desktop resolution (1920x1080)' (measured, screenshot 02); it is still not selectable. WINQUAKE.EXE's menu is selectable, but only for 8-bpp modes with w<=1280 and h<=1024 (cmp 0x500/0x400 at 0x40c83d).
Quake1.evidence: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Quake1/Play Quake.bat; provisioning/fleetres/fleetres.c 787-821; .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/{123,145,195,240}-fleetres-caps.txt (deployed FLEETRES.EXE -cmd -cap 1280 960, -info, DISPLAYCFG); .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/123-glquake-current/05-window-console-describemodes.png + 05b-describemodes-zoom.png + q1enum-transcript.txt (GLQuake's own 29-slot list on .123); .../123-glquake-current/01-gdi-attract.png, 02-gdi-video-options.png, 03-engine-F11-attract-quake02.png, 04-engine-F11-videomodes-quake03.png, q1cur-transcript.txt (-current proof on .123: WINLIST GLQuake/WinQuake 0,0-1920x1080, DISPLAYCFG 1920x1080x32 before/during/after, engine TGAs 1920x1080 = 6,220,818 B); .../123-glquake-modelist/123-glquake-qconsole.log + q1-transcript.txt (the -condebug run that exited right after the 3.8 KB GL_EXTENSIONS line); .../static/glquake-condebug-and-conwidth.txt (Con_DebugLog 1 KB static at 0x45c580 directly before con_text 0x45c980; R_SetupGL scales vrect by glwidth/vid.width; -conwidth/-conheight at 0x4160e1); prior agent's .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/disasm/*.
Quake1.fix: Launcher change using stock switches, VERIFIED on .123 hardware (the switches were typed by hand, not run through a launcher): GLQUAKE.EXE -current -conwidth %FR_CONW% -conheight %FR_CONH% +fov %FR_FOV%, where FR_CONW=FR_W/2 and FR_CONH=FR_H/2 are computed per box. That gives 960x540 on the 1080p LCDs and 512x384 on a 1024x768 CRT. FR_W/H must come from an UNCAPPED FLEETRES call. Use -current only when FR_LIVE_W x FR_LIVE_H equals that FR_W x FR_H. Otherwise keep TODAY's capped call (-cap 1280 960, i.e. 800x600, which is proven), so call FLEETRES twice or save the capped values separately. The .123 run was `-current -conwidth 960 -conheight 540 +fov 106`. It gave a borderless GLQuake window at 0,0-1920x1080, the desktop mode never changed, engine F11 frames came out 1920x1080 with proportionate geometry and a 2x HUD, and the Video Modes page showed 'Desktop resolution (1920x1080)'. Three corrections to the prior proposal. (1) Hardcoding -conwidth 960 -conheight 540 is wrong. -current also fires on the 4:3 CRT boxes, and R_SetupGL projects from vid (= con) coordinates, so a 16:9 console there squashes the picture horizontally. (2) The fallback must not be an uncapped -width %FR_W43% -height %FR_H43% -bpp 32. 1280x960x32 is slot 20 on .123, but on .240 (and possibly .195) it falls outside the 29 slots, and a miss is a hard Sys_Error. (3) There is no selectable in-game resolution control with stock GLQuake or WinQuake. Only a port such as QuakeSpasm gives one. None is on the share: a case-insensitive find over Files, Utility, DiskImages and transmission found none.
Quake1.fix_source: Already in the staged GLQUAKE.EXE: '-current' @0x450e20 (code 0x415e3d sets modelist[1] from GetSystemMetrics, vid_default=1 and leavecurrentmode [0x8094a0]=1; VID_SetFullDIBMode @0x414470 then skips ChangeDisplaySettingsA), '-conwidth'/'-conheight' @0x450de0/0x450dd4, and 'Desktop resolution (%dx%d)'. The launcher text is generated by scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py (NEW_GLQUAKE, and the GLQUAKE.EXE branch of new_launcher that emits call_cap(1280, 960)). FR_CONW/FR_CONH can be computed with set /a in the launcher, or added to fleetres.c followed by a FLEETRES.EXE rebuild and re-stage. A selectable in-game menu would need a port download (QuakeSpasm, sourceforge); none is on the share.
Quake1.fix_risk: Low. -current is a borderless window at the live desktop mode, not an exclusive mode set. The window covered the screen on .123 and the taskbar was hidden. No mode change happens at start, so nothing needs restoring on exit. On alt-tab back, AppActivate calls ChangeDisplaySettings with an empty gdevmode, which should be harmless (not tested). Unmeasured: Win7 .195 (DWM), .145, .240, and the Voodoo 5 box .124, where 'Play Quake - Voodoo.bat' calls 'Play Quake.bat' on a VSA-100 and so reaches -current through the Glide-backed ICD. The protocol is unchanged, so the NetQuake server at 192.168.1.132:26000 is unaffected (join not re-tested). Tests to change in the same commit: tests/python/test_fleetres_staging.py test_only_the_measured_ceilings_carry_a_cap and test_glquake_cap_is_the_measured_ceiling_not_the_old_guess. PROCESS RISK THAT BIT THIS REVIEW: every LCD box was in use by other agents' game tests, and two of my launches on .123 minimized other agents' sessions (details in verifier_notes).
Quake1.hw_check: Only on an idle box: check WINLIST and PROCLIST immediately before launching, and never chain the check and the launch in one command. (1) Today: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Quake1" "Play Quake.bat"; DISPLAYCFG get should read 800x600x32. (2) Mode list: GLQUAKE.EXE -window -width 1280 -height 960 -conwidth 1280 -conheight 960 +toggleconsole +vid_describemodes, then SCREENSHOT 0 (done on .123). DO NOT use the prior proposal's -condebug + qconsole.log route. Con_DebugLog vsprintf's into a 1 KB static buffer that sits directly before the console-text pointer, and GL_EXTENSIONS is 3.8 KB on .123. The -condebug run there exited within 9 s, right after logging that line. (3) Fix proof: -current -conwidth <FR_W/2> -conheight <FR_H/2> +fov <FR_FOV>. WINLIST must show GLQuake at 0,0-1920x1080 and DISPLAYCFG must stay 1920x1080x32. Press F11: id1\quakeNN.tga must be 6,220,818 B (1920x1080). Then keys (they work fullscreen): ESCAPE, DOWN, DOWN, RETURN, UP, RETURN; the Video Modes page must read 'Desktop resolution (1920x1080)'. Then connect 192.168.1.132. Repeat on .145, .240 and .195; on .195, use the F11 TGA if GDI comes back black. Clean up: taskkill /f /im "GLQUAKE.EXE" and DELETE the new TGAs (quake00/01.tga on .123 predate this review).
Quake1.verifier_notes: CONFIRMED on hardware: the launch_sets numbers (800x600 on all four, from the deployed FLEETRES.EXE), the read-only menu, the 30-slot cap (measured list on .123 ends at slot 29 = 1920x1080x16), and -current (verified working at 1920x1080 on .123). CHANGED: (a) the fix: per-box -conwidth/-conheight instead of 960x540; fallback = keep the proven cap, not an uncapped -bpp 32 request. (b) fix_risk: the prior text said the read-only menu 'keeps the old label on mode 1'. It actually shows 'Desktop resolution (1920x1080)' for every entry (measured). (c) hw_check: removed -condebug, which crashes GLQuake (measured exit plus disassembly). (d) menu_source: the enumeration order is per driver (ATI .123 resolution-major, measured), so which 1080p depth fits varies by box. DISCLOSURE: at about 00:33:30 and about 00:54:30 EDT my windowed GLQuake launches on .123 took focus from other agents' Carmageddon II (pid 1468) and Descent 3 (pid 1864) fullscreen sessions. Both windows were minimized and the desktop returned to 1920x1080. Evidence those agents captured in those minutes is disturbed, not a game fault. I sent the orchestrator (main) a message about it, then stopped launching on shared boxes.

Quake2Complete.title: Quake2Complete
Quake2Complete.engine: id Tech 2: retail Quake II 3.20 (quake2.exe md5 57dd2cf4ba176f3e6ae72fccc94c38b4, 'Oct 16 1998 Win32 RELEASE'; ref_gl.dll b6d33427..., ref_soft.dll 203dc879...), with baseq2, xatrix, rogue and ctf. A second 3.20 copy under Files/Games/Windows XP/Quake2 differs only in the DOS stub (aea5be5f...).
Quake2Complete.launch_sets: 1280x960 fullscreen (gl_mode 8) on all four LCDs. Each of the 4 launchers calls FLEETRES with no cap, writes <mod>\fleetres.cfg (set gl_mode "%FR_Q2MODE%" plus vid_fullscreen 1), and passes +set gl_mode %FR_Q2MODE%. The autoexec.cfg in baseq2, xatrix, rogue and ctf each ends with exec fleetres.cfg (checked all four). The GAMERES idtech2 rule (gameres.h 702-705, body 867-870) writes the same file. Re-measured today: the deployed FLEETRES.EXE -info reports q2mode 8 on .123, .145, .195 and .240, and GAMERES target.q2mode is 8 on all four. Measured 1280x960 on .123, .240 and .246/.195 (the .246 F11 TGA is 1280x960). The only 1024x768 record, .145 on 2026-09-01, predates today's values. Deployed launchers equal staged. 1280x960 is 4:3, so the panel scaler stretches or pillarboxes it.
Quake2Complete.menu_source: Hardcoded in quake2.exe. vid_modes[] is at file offset 0x543d0: exactly 10 entries of {desc,w,h,mode}, 'Mode 0: 320x240'..'Mode 9: 1600x1200'; entry [10] is not a mode. The Video menu's 'video mode' spinner uses a separate label-pointer array at file offset 0x54678: '[320 240  ]'..'[1600 1200]' then NULL (10 labels). The menu index IS gl_mode. ref_gl gets its size only via Vid_GetModeInfo(gl_mode). There is no custom mode and no 16:9 entry.
Quake2Complete.evidence: .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/menus/idtech2_vid_modes_tables.txt and quake2_320_modes_and_menu.txt (offsets re-checked with pefile: table at 0x543d0, 10 entries; label array at 0x54678); .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/{123,145,195,240}-fleetres-caps.txt (q2mode 8 on all four); /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Quake2Complete/Quake II*.bat and {baseq2,xatrix,rogue,ctf}/autoexec.cfg; agent/shared/gameres.h 295-330, 470, 702-705, 867-870; compat records in .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/compat_render_measured.txt.
Quake2Complete.fix: There is no config-only route in 3.20. Byte-patch Quake2Complete's quake2.exe only: vid_modes[9] width @0x54464 1600->1920 and height @0x54468 1200->1080, plus the same-length strings 'Mode 9: 1600x1200'->'Mode 9: 1920x1080' and label '[1600 1200]'->'[1920 1080]' (file offset 0x54720). No fleet box uses gl_mode 9 today; the CRT boxes resolve to 4, 6 or 8. ADDITION the prior answer glossed over: FR_Q2MODE feeds three titles (Quake2Complete x4, SiNGold x3 including the software sw_mode launcher, SoF x1). Choosing 9 for a 1920x1080 target therefore needs a NEW, separately named value (for example FR_Q2WIDE), not a change to FR_Q2MODE. The same value must be added identically in fleetres.c and gameres.h, and both the launchers and the GAMERES idtech2 body must use it. The two writers of <mod>\fleetres.cfg would otherwise rewrite each other on every sync (tests/python/test_gameres_mirror.py, test_a_shared_cfg_is_written_identically_by_both_writers). Add set fov %FR_FOV% to both writers as well. Alternative client: Yamagi Quake II (r_mode -1 plus a real video menu). It speaks protocol 34 like the fleet's Yamagi 8.60 server. An XP-buildable fork exists (web-verified: github.com/akosela/yquake2-xp, forked from 8.01); whether it ships release binaries is unverified. No Yamagi, KMQuake2, Q2PRO or R1Q2 build is on the share (case-insensitive search).
Quake2Complete.fix_source: The patch needs no download: the bytes are in the staged quake2.exe at the offsets above. The selection logic lives in provisioning/fleetres/fleetres.c and agent/shared/gameres.h. FLEETRES.EXE must be rebuilt and re-staged into every title by scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py. gameres.h is compiled into the agent, so the agent needs a version bump and publish. Yamagi-XP would have to be downloaded from github.com/akosela/yquake2-xp, together with Yamagi-built game DLLs for baseq2, xatrix, rogue and ctf.
Quake2Complete.fix_risk: The patch modifies a retail exe shared by 4 launchers. 3.20 draws the HUD, console and menus at 1:1 pixels, so they are tiny at 1080p. Never point ref_soft at mode 9 (the id GPL ref_soft MAXWIDTH is 1600; source knowledge, not binary-verified). Quake2Win9x ships the identical exe; leave that copy stock. ROLLOUT RISK: until every box runs an agent with the new gameres.h, an old agent writes gl_mode 8 and a new launcher writes 9 into the same fleetres.cfg on each sync. The launcher writes last and also passes +set, so the game still starts at 9, but GAMERES never settles to '0 value(s) changed' during the rollout. Multiplayer: protocol 34 has no exe or pure check, so a join to 192.168.1.132:27910 should be unaffected; prove it with one join.
Quake2Complete.hw_check: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Quake2Complete" "Quake II.bat" on an idle box; DISPLAYCFG get should read 1280x960. The menu is keyboard-navigable: Esc > Options > Video, then the arrow keys cycle 'video mode'. Press F11 for baseq2\scrnshot\quakeNN.tga, or use GDI SCREENSHOT 0 on the XP boxes. The list should end at [1600 1200]. After the patch: the last entry should read [1920 1080], applying it should give DISPLAYCFG 1920x1080 and a 1920x1080 frame, `connect 192.168.1.132:27910` should still join, and two consecutive GAMESYNC/GAMERES APPLY runs should report 0 value(s) changed.
Quake2Complete.verifier_notes: Confirmed (table and label offsets re-checked; q2mode 8 re-measured on all four boxes; every mod's autoexec ends with exec fleetres.cfg). Added: FR_Q2MODE feeds three titles, so a separate value is needed and it must change identically in fleetres.c and gameres.h (both write fleetres.cfg), with the agent-rollout churn noted; the Yamagi XP fork is web-verified. The prior note is correct that the staged autoexec comment's 'autoexec runs BEFORE VID_Init' is wrong: in id's CL_Init, FS_ExecAutoexec runs after VID_Init.

HexenII.title: HexenII
HexenII.engine: Raven Hexen II retail 1.03. glh2.exe is a GLQuake-derived OpenGL build (md5 c450ea8ac9aefa9e4a5b48e9c7ae4e66, 'Exe: 15:08:09 Sep 4 1997'; VOODOO\GLH2.EXE is identical). h2.exe is the software build (md5 7ad8abed...).
HexenII.launch_sets: Not 1080p, and it differs by box. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-29: the deployed C:\Games\HexenII\FLEETRES.EXE -cmd -cap 1024 768 returns FR_W/H=848x480 on .123 and .240, and 1024x768 on .145 and .195. The Play, Host and Join launchers pass glh2.exe -width %FR_W% -height %FR_H% with no -bpp, so glh2 tries 15 bpp, then 16. The compat DB measured 848x480 on .123/.240 and 1024x768x16 on .246/.195 (DISPLAYCFG). The deployed launchers equal the staged ones. There is no GAMERES rule. The 2026-08-31 -cap was added to the share outside the generator: stage-fleetres.py TITLES['HexenII'] has no cap, and test_hexen2_is_not_capped_like_glquake pins that. `stage-fleetres.py --check` still reports all 213 launchers as current (run today; its 1 failure is Thief2), so it cannot see this drift. PER-TITLE-STATUS's '1080p, measured on .145' predates the cap.
HexenII.menu_source: Options > Video Modes is the same READ-ONLY GLQuake page (the 'Fullscreen Modes (WIDTHxHEIGHTxBPP)' and 'Video modes must be set from the...' strings are in glh2.exe). Its entries are the driver-enumerated modelist with the same 30-slot cap (cmp ecx,0x1e at 0x4308e2). That explains both measurements: .240 refused 1280x960, 1280x1024 and 1920x1080, while .145 accepted 1920x1080 at 16 bpp. The same enumeration, measured for GLQuake on .123, is resolution-major and ends at 1920x1080x16. What appears differs by box, and nothing on the page can be selected. With -current the entries become 'Desktop resolution (%dx%d)' (the string is in glh2). h2.exe's menu is selectable but takes 8-bpp modes only, w<=1280, h<=1024 (0x415e6d).
HexenII.evidence: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/HexenII/{Play Hexen II.bat, Host Hexen II - LAN.bat, Join Hexen II - LAN.bat} (-cap 1024 768); .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/{123,145,195,240}-fleetres-caps.txt; .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/static/glh2-current-and-projection.txt (-current at 0x430e32 sets vid_default [0x4680a8] and leavecurrentmode [0x7cb948]; VID_SetFullDIBMode 0x42f550 skips ChangeDisplaySettings when it is set; vid 320x200 fixed at 0x42f708; R_SetupGL 0x407bb0 projection); .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/disasm/hexen2_modelist_cap30.txt; scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py 1038-1060; tests/python/test_lan_multiplayer_library.py 44-99 and test_fleetres_staging.py 739-746.
HexenII.fix: Launch change: glh2.exe -current -heapsize 32768 -nocdaudio (plus the Host/Join extras). This is statically confirmed: the -current path sets leavecurrentmode [0x7cb948] and VID_SetFullDIBMode skips ChangeDisplaySettings, the same code as GLQuake, whose -current I verified on .123. Guard it with FR_LIVE == FR_W/H from an UNCAPPED FLEETRES call. CORRECTION: the fallback must keep today's -cap 1024 768 path, which is measured working. It must not be an uncapped -width %FR_W43% -height %FR_H43% (1280x960), because that was measured failing on .240 with 'Specified video mode not available'. The failure happens before the listen server opens, so the Host LAN launcher would silently host nothing. -current can never hit that check. NEW FINDING on aspect (static): glh2 has no -conwidth switch at all. Its vid is fixed at 320x200 (0x42f708). R_SetupGL scales vrect by glwidth/320 and glheight/200 and calls MYgluPerspective(fovy=2*atan(h/w), aspect=w/h) on that 320x200-space vrect (constant 114.59=360/pi at 0x45a130). So horizontal FOV is always 90, the fov cvar is ignored, and the picture is correct only on 16:10. It is about 11% horizontally stretched at 16:9 (1920x1080 via -current, and today's 848x480) and about 17% horizontally squashed at 4:3 (today's 1024x768 on .145/.195). -current improves resolution and error size but cannot fix the aspect. Only a port (uHexen2 / Hammer of Thyrion) gives a correct aspect and an in-game resolution menu; none is on the share (case-insensitive search for hexen2, uhexen2, thyrion, glhexen).
HexenII.fix_source: -current is already in the staged glh2.exe (string @0x468a48). The launcher recipe lives in scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py TITLES['HexenII']; its 'fix' list must also cover the -cap text, which was added outside the generator. A port would need downloading (uHexen2 1.5.x, sourceforge.net/projects/uhexen2).
HexenII.fix_risk: Low to medium. It is a stock switch but depends on the live desktop mode (hence the guard). The 11% 16:9 stretch is inherent to this 1997 build (static finding, unmeasured). LAN: the tests test_hexen2_gl_launchers_cap_to_a_mode_the_engine_has and _cap_the_engine_at_1024x768 require the cap and must be rewritten alongside. The latter's docstring claims -cap 1024 768 yields FR_W=1024 FR_H=768 on hardware, which is false on .123/.240 (848x480, re-measured today). Its assertion only checks the cap numbers. Host and join must be re-proven on two boxes with scripts/game-servers/nqquery.py <ip> 26900 HEXENII. .124's Voodoo launcher calls 'Play Hexen II.bat' on a VSA-100 and would inherit -current (unmeasured).
HexenII.hw_check: On an idle box: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\HexenII" "Play Hexen II.bat"; DISPLAYCFG get should read 848x480 on .123/.240 and 1024x768x16 on .145/.195. The menu is keyboard-navigable: Esc > Options > Video Modes. The GL build's F11 writes data1\shots\hexenNN.TGA ('shots/hexen00.tga' in glh2), not .pcx as the README says; on XP, GDI SCREENSHOT 0 also works. Fix proof: glh2.exe -current -heapsize 32768 -nocdaudio. WINLIST should show class HexenII at 0,0-1920x1080, DISPLAYCFG should stay 1920x1080x32, the frame should be 1920x1080, and a round object should look about 11% wide. Then Host with -current on one box, confirm nqquery.py <ip> 26900 HEXENII answers, join from a second box, and screenshot both. Delete the new TGAs and taskkill /f /im "glh2.exe".
HexenII.verifier_notes: Launch_sets confirmed on hardware (848x480 on .123/.240, 1024x768 on .145/.195 from the deployed FLEETRES.EXE). -current confirmed by disassembly: the prior evidence file showed only the vid_default store, and I located the leavecurrentmode store and the check in VID_SetFullDIBMode. CHANGED: (1) the fallback keeps the measured cap instead of an uncapped FR_W43 request; (2) the 'aspect unknown' note is replaced by a static finding that the fixed 320x200 virtual screen means an 11% stretch at 16:9 and a 17% squash at 4:3, with the fov cvar ignored; (3) the screenshot is TGA not PCX; (4) the test's FR_W=1024 claim lives in its docstring, not its assertion. No hardware run of glh2 -current: every LCD box was busy with other agents' tests.

SiNGold.title: SiNGold
SiNGold.engine: Ritual SiN (id Tech 2 derivative) at the official 1.11 (sin.exe md5 8d320d7fc3ea3a226ec98dafef3e81ba, 'Jan 22 2001'), with Wages of SiN (2015\) and ctf\. The GOG 1.13b rebuild that was replaced is kept in _patches (see fix_source).
SiNGold.launch_sets: 1280x960 fullscreen (gl_mode 8) through Play SiN Gold.bat and Play Wages of SiN.bat. Each calls FLEETRES, writes base\ or 2015\fleetres.cfg (gl_mode %FR_Q2MODE% plus vid_fullscreen), and passes +set gl_mode. Both autoexec.cfg files set gl_mode 6 and end with exec fleetres.cfg, so 8 wins. GAMERES idtech2 rows cover base and 2015. FR_Q2MODE is 8 on all four boxes (re-measured). Measured 1280x960 on .123/.240 (verified) and .246/.195 (runs). Deployed launchers equal staged. .145 crashes in every OpenGL context (README-CDCHECK: the log ends at GL_VERSION 3.3.0, before GL_EXTENSIONS), so only 'Play SiN - software renderer.bat' works there. CORRECTION: that launcher's +set sw_mode %FR_Q2MODE% (8) does not survive. It is an EARLY +set, base\autoexec.cfg runs later and sets sw_mode "6" (line 107), and the software launcher writes no fleetres.cfg (fleetres.cfg sets only gl_mode anyway). The software path therefore settles at mode 6 = 1024x768, which matches the verified .145 run (static inference from the Quake II startup order, not re-measured).
SiNGold.menu_source: Menu data file menus/main.mnu, used at 640x480 and above (sin.exe 0x429c3a: width>=0x280 and height>=0x1e0 selects main.mnu, else main_alt.mnu). Path: main menu > Controls > Video > 'Video Mode:', listitem con_vidmode. base\pak5.sin (1.11) has numitems 10, ' 320 x 240'..' 1600 x 1200'. 2015\pak0.sin has numitems 9, so Wages stops at 1280 x 960. ctf\pak1.sin carries its own 10-item copy. apply_vid_changes copies con_vidmode into gl_mode and sw_mode, which index sin.exe's vid_modes (file offset 0x94450, Mode 0 320x240 .. Mode 9 1600x1200, 10 entries).
SiNGold.evidence: .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/menus/sin_main_mnu_video_mode.txt and idtech2_vid_modes_tables.txt (table re-checked); .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/static/sin-menu-sync.txt (menu_main 0x44a8e0 -> vid_reset 0x44a050: con_vidmode=gl_mode when vid_ref is 'gl'; main vs main_alt at 0x429c3a; FS_AddGameDirectory 0x441ef0: pak0-31 then the loose directory PREPENDED, so loose files win); .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/static/sin-gog-1.13b-widescreen-table.txt; /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/SiNGold/{Play SiN Gold.bat, Play Wages of SiN.bat, Play SiN - software renderer.bat, base/autoexec.cfg 61-64,106-108,177, 2015/autoexec.cfg 73-76,118-120,189, README-RESTAGE.txt, README-CDCHECK.txt}; gameres.h 706-707.
SiNGold.fix: Same shape as Quake II. Patch 1.11 sin.exe vid_modes[9]: width @0x944e4 1600->1920, height @0x944e8 1200->1080, string 'Mode 9: 1600x1200'->'Mode 9: 1920x1080'. Relabel the menu, but NO PAK IS NEEDED, which corrects the prior 'pak required (inferred)'. SiN's FS_AddGameDirectory loads pak0-31 and then prepends the loose directory, so loose files override that directory's paks. Ship loose base\menus\main.mnu (copy of pak5's, ' 1600 x 1200'->' 1920 x 1080') and 2015\menus\main.mnu (copy of 2015\pak0's, same relabel plus numitems 9->10). main_alt.mnu only matters below 640x480. Then implement the separate 1080p gl_mode value identically in FLEETRES and GAMERES (see Quake2Complete). Keep the software launcher off mode 9; today its sw_mode is overridden to 6 anyway. REFUTED: the prior claim that 'No SiN widescreen fix is on the share'. The GOG SiN Gold 1.13b rebuild on the share already has a widescreen table: 'Mode 0: 640x480' .. 'Mode 11: 1280x720 (Widescreen)', 'Mode 12: 1920x1080 (Widescreen)' .. 'Mode 14: 3840x2160'. It is NOT usable as-is. It is an MSVC-2015 build with subsystem/OS 6.0, which XP's loader refuses. It imports VCRUNTIME140 and api-ms-win-crt-*, needs SSE2 libm, and its mode numbers differ from 1.11's. README-RESTAGE records that on Win7 .246 it 'exits immediately with RC=0' (cause never found). At most it is a lead for .195 only. UNTESTED LEAD for .145's GL crash (without it the 1080p patch never reaches that box): NVIDIA's per-application OpenGL 'Extension limit' control-panel setting targets exactly this class of old id-lineage crash on long extension strings. Its availability on .145's driver is unverified.
SiNGold.fix_source: No download: the bytes are in the staged sin.exe, the menus are in base\pak5.sin and 2015\pak0.sin (extract, edit, ship loose). The GOG build is at /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/_patches/backup-2026-08-29/SiNGold/gog-1.13b-binaries/sin.exe (md5 131399874914033b73d439733663dc47) and in Files/Games/Windows XP/setup_sin_gold_1.13b_(36951).exe.
SiNGold.fix_risk: Medium. It modifies the 1.11 exe, the same file that solved the CD check; keep the original. SiN's menus and HUD are laid out for 4:3 and are unmeasured at 16:9. Never send ref_soft_real.dll to mode 9. The same FLEETRES/GAMERES lockstep and rollout risk as Quake II applies. Multiplayer is box-to-box via ds_*.bat with no pure check; prove one join. The video-menu presets (vm_hw_low/mid/high.cfg) set gl_mode 2 or 3 and vid_restart, so clicking one drops to 512x384 or 640x480 until the next launch.
SiNGold.hw_check: On an idle box other than .145: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\SiNGold" "Play SiN Gold.bat"; DISPLAYCFG get should read 1280x960. Menu path: main menu > Controls > Video > 'Video Mode:'. It should show ' 1280 x 960' (menu_main runs vid_reset, which copies gl_mode into con_vidmode) and end at ' 1600 x 1200', or at ' 1280 x 960' in Wages of SiN. Keyboard navigation of this menu is still unproven on the fleet. F11 writes base\players\<name>\scrnshot\sin###.tga; on XP, GDI SCREENSHOT 0 also works. On .145, check the software shortcut: DISPLAYCFG should read 1024x768 (not 1280x960).
SiNGold.verifier_notes: CHANGED: (1) The prior verifier note ('menu shows 1024 x 768 while running 1280x960; Apply drops to 1024x768') is refuted by disassembly, not measured. The menu_main command (0x44a8e0) calls vid_reset (0x44a050), which sets con_vidmode from gl_mode under vid_ref gl, so the list shows the running mode and Apply keeps it. (2) 'A pak is required, loose files are shadowed' is wrong for SiN: its file system searches the loose directory first; it is right for SoF. (3) The software-renderer launch_sets was corrected: autoexec's sw_mode 6 wins, giving 1024x768, not 1280x960. (4) 'No SiN widescreen fix on the share' was corrected: the GOG 1.13b build has a 1920x1080 mode but is not viable on XP. (5) Added the .145 extension-limit lead. Table offsets and menu contents confirmed.

SoldierOfFortune.title: SoldierOfFortune
SoldierOfFortune.engine: Raven Soldier of Fortune (id Tech 2 + GHOUL). It shows 1.03 x86F on screen (SoF.exe md5 2f4db3771d51d8b585bbea695041e40c). The last official patch, 1.07f, is not on the share; Files/Games/Windows XP/Soldier of Fortune (2000).zip is only the CD image (bin/cue).
SoldierOfFortune.launch_sets: 1280x960 fullscreen (gl_mode 8). Play Soldier of Fortune.bat calls FLEETRES, writes base\fleetres.cfg (gl_mode %FR_Q2MODE% plus vid_fullscreen), and passes +set gl_mode. base\autoexec.cfg ends with exec fleetres.cfg. The GAMERES idtech2 row covers base. FR_Q2MODE is 8 on all four boxes (re-measured). Measured 1280x960 on .123 (verified, ARC menu) and .240 (runs, window 0,0-1280x960); .246/.195 runs with the resolution unrecorded; .145 has no record. The deployed launcher equals the staged one. No level loads anywhere: every map raises the WON 'insert the SOF CD' error (requires.json, re-measured 2026-09-28 on .124), so only the menus can be verified at any resolution.
SoldierOfFortune.menu_source: RMF text menu menus/m_video.rmf, only in base\pak0.pak (pak1.pak holds no menus): <list "640x480,800x600,960x720,1024x768,1152x864,1280x960,1600x1200" match "3,4,5,6,7,8,9" cvar menu_mode>. Opening the video menu runs menus/video.cfg (set menu_mode $gl_mode), so the list shows the running mode. 'Apply' runs menus/applyvid.cfg (set gl_mode $menu_mode; vid_restart). SoF.exe's vid_modes table at file offset 0x1c6e08 holds 'Mode 0/1/2: Unsupported' (320x240, 400x300, 512x384), then 'Mode 3: 640x480'..'Mode 9: 1600x1200'.
SoldierOfFortune.evidence: .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/menus/sof_m_video_rmf.txt and idtech2_vid_modes_tables.txt (re-checked); .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/static/sof-fs-order-and-menu-sync.txt (FS_AddGameDirectory: loose directory first, then pak0-9 prepended, so paks win; menus/video.cfg); /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/SoldierOfFortune/{Play Soldier of Fortune.bat, base/autoexec.cfg, README-FLEET.txt, requires.json}; web: sof1.megalag.org/widescreen/ and sof1.megalag.org/sofplus/.
SoldierOfFortune.fix: (a) In-tree: patch SoF.exe vid_modes[9] (width @0x1c6e9c 1600->1920, height @0x1c6ea0 1200->1080). Ship base\pak2.pak with an edited menus/m_video.rmf (relabel '1600x1200' as '1920x1080', mapped to 9). A pak IS required here: SoF adds the loose directory first and then prepends pak0-9, so a loose m_video.rmf would be shadowed by pak0.pak. pak2 is within the 0-9 loop. Then use the separate 1080p mode value in FLEETRES and GAMERES in lockstep (see Quake2Complete). (b) The community route, web-verified: SoF 1.07f plus the SoFplus client, whose _sp_cl_vid_mode_0.._9 cvars redefine the modes and whose video menu is overhauled. SoFplus requires 1.07f, and neither is on the share. megalag's own SoF.exe widescreen patch, which does option (a), warns that the bottom of stock menus gets cut off, horizontal FOV stays fixed (vert-), and anti-cheat may complain. It recommends SoFplus instead. Either way, gameplay at 1080p cannot be shown until the WON CD check is solved.
SoldierOfFortune.fix_source: (a) No download: the bytes are in the staged SoF.exe, and the menu is in base\pak0.pak. (b) Would need the SoF 1.07f patch and the SoFplus client from sof1.megalag.org. A case-insensitive share search found only the CD image, SoF_Demo.exe and SoF2 material.
SoldierOfFortune.fix_risk: Menus clipped at 16:9 (web-reported); FOV fixed (vert-); the exe patch may upset obsolete anti-cheat. There is no multiplayer regression, since multiplayer is already blocked (WON error, no SoF server on the host). Moving to 1.07f changes the version every box presents, so patch the library and move all boxes together.
SoldierOfFortune.hw_check: On an idle box: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\SoldierOfFortune" "Play Soldier of Fortune.bat"; DISPLAYCFG get should read 1280x960. Menu: ARC globe > options folder > Video > 'Resolution', which should read 1280x960. Input evidence conflicts: absolute UICLICK worked on .123, but on .240 the cursor moved by deltas and UIKEY reached nothing. Treat it as needing a human unless a first UICLICK moves the cursor to the clicked point. F11 writes user\scrnshot\sof00.tga (SoF.exe writes under './user'; the staged tree ships user\scrnshot\, and the autoexec comment's base\scrnshot is stale). On XP, GDI SCREENSHOT 0 also works.
SoldierOfFortune.verifier_notes: Confirmed (tables, RMF, launch values re-measured, compat records). Added: the pak requirement is correct for SoF, established by the file-system search order in the disassembly. The menu syncs menu_mode from gl_mode on open, so there is no stale-label problem. The screenshot path is user\scrnshot. The prior agent's web claims (SoFplus cvars, 1.07f requirement, menu cut-off, anti-cheat warning) were re-verified on sof1.megalag.org.

Doom3.title: Doom3
Doom3.engine: id Tech 4: official DOOM 3 1.3 (version.inf ExtVersion=1.3; DOOM3.exe md5 7cd77c22b38c223ef1047083e374875a, 5,832,704 B, no SafeDisc). base/gamex86.dll (md5 e06f4eb6...) is byte-identical to game03.pk4's 2005-05-10 build. CORRECTION: Resurrection of Evil is NOT installed. d3xp/ holds only the 1.3 patch's overlay: game01-03.pk4 (game DLLs) and pak001.pk4 (99,336 B: mainmenu.gui, mpmain.gui, efx files, one mtr). The RoE content pak (d3xp/pak000.pk4, several hundred MB) is absent from the library and from .123 and .145 (DIRLIST).
Doom3.launch_sets: 1920x1080 on all four LCDs. Play DOOM 3.bat and Host DOOM 3 - LAN.bat call FLEETRES with no cap and run DOOM3.exe +set r_mode -1 +set r_customWidth %FR_W% +set r_customHeight %FR_H% +set r_aspectRatio %FR_D3AR% +set r_fullscreen 1 (FR_D3AR=1 on 16:9). FR_W/H=1920x1080 on all four (re-measured with the deployed FLEETRES.EXE -info). id Tech 4 re-applies +set after DoomConfig.cfg. r_aspectRatio is defined only in the game DLL (0 hits in DOOM3.exe, 1 in gamex86.dll), and the command-line value survives the DLL's later registration. Measured: 1920x1080 verified on .123 and .240 (2026-08-31), DISPLAYCFG 1920x1080x32 on .246/.195. .145: DOOM 3 has NEVER been started there (C:\Games\Doom3\base has no DoomConfig.cfg and no config.spec). Unexplained observation: .123's DoomConfig.cfg (written 2026-09-01 04:49:59) archives r_mode "3" with r_customWidth/Height 1920/1080 and no r_aspectRatio line. So the last session there ended at r_mode 3, from either a menu touch or R_InitOpenGL's safe-mode fallback. The next launch still passes r_mode -1. Launchers equal staged. Doom3 is still deployed on .240 although today's gate refuses it there for disk (1490 < 1600 MB).
Doom3.menu_source: base/pak007.pk4 guis/mainmenu.gui (the effective copy, lines 4888-4891) System > 'Screen Size' (#str_02153): choiceDef OS2Primary { choices "#str_04222" values "3;4;5;6;7;8" cvar "r_mode" choiceType 1 }. strings/english.lang: #str_04222 = "640x480;800x600;1024x768;1152x864;1280x1024;1600x1200". DOOM3.exe r_vidModes run from Mode 0 320x240 to Mode 8 1600x1200. There is no aspect control ('aspect' does not occur in the GUI). With r_mode -1, idChoiceWindow falls back to index 0 and shows '640x480' (per id's GPL choice-window logic; not measured). d3xp/pak001.pk4 carries the same choiceDef but is inert without RoE.
Doom3.evidence: .claude/evidence-1080p/static-idtech12-doom3/menus/doom3_mainmenu_screensize.txt (re-extracted from base/pak007.pk4, identical); .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/static/doom3-d3xp-and-config.txt; .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/123-Doom3-DoomConfig.cfg (DOWNLOADed from .123); .claude/evidence-1080p/review-idtech12-doom3/{123,145,195,240}-fleetres-caps.txt; /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Doom3/{Play DOOM 3.bat, Host DOOM 3 - LAN.bat, version.inf, d3xp/}; scripts/game-servers/doom3/entry.sh (si_pure 0).
Doom3.fix: Ship base/zz_fleetvideo.pk4, which sorts after pak007.pk4 (Doom 3 prepends pk4s in sorted order, so later names win). It holds a copy of pak007's guis/mainmenu.gui with only the Screen Size choiceDef edited: choices '640x480;800x600;1024x768;1152x864;1280x1024;1600x1200;Native', values '3;4;5;6;7;8;-1'. Use 'Native' rather than '1920x1080', because r_customWidth/Height are per box. Add one choiceDef on r_aspectRatio (choices '4:3;16:9;16:10', values '0;1;2'); that cvar is registered by the game DLL, which is loaded while the menu runs. DROPPED from the prior proposal: d3xp/zz_fleetvideo.pk4. RoE is not installed, so there is nothing to override there until the RoE content pak is staged. No existing fix is on the share: DOOM 3 UPDATE 1.3.exe and classic_doom_3_v1.1.exe are the only related files, dhewm3 is absent and not network-compatible with 1.3, and D3EE is absent.
Doom3.fix_source: No download: it edits guis/mainmenu.gui from base/pak007.pk4 (696,570 B) and packages it into a new pk4.
Doom3.fix_risk: Low to medium. It replaces a ~700 KB id GUI script with a copy; diff it against the original so only that choiceDef changes. The fleet doom3-server runs si_pure 0, so an extra client pk4 is fine. On a pure server, client-only paks are excluded and the stock menu returns. The HUD and menus stay 640x480-virtual and stretch at 16:9 (cosmetic). Choosing 'Native' needs r_customWidth/Height already archived; the launcher's +set archives them on the first exit, so .145, which has never run the game, gets them on its first run.
Doom3.hw_check: On an idle box: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Doom3" "Play DOOM 3.bat"; DISPLAYCFG get should read 1920x1080x32. Run it on .145 first, where it has never been run. The menu uses a mouse cursor and is expected to be relative-mouse, so it needs a human unless one UICLICK test proves otherwise. Keyboard-only check: Ctrl+Alt+~, query r_mode, r_customWidth, r_customHeight and r_aspectRatio, run listModes, `condump fleetres_check.txt`, then DOWNLOAD C:\Games\Doom3\base\fleetres_check.txt. On XP boxes, GDI SCREENSHOT 0 captures fullscreen GL, so the Screen Size control can be photographed directly. After the pk4 fix, the Screen Size control must read 'Native' while r_mode is -1. Then DOWNLOAD DoomConfig.cfg after a clean quit and check that r_mode is archived as -1 (it is 3 on .123 today). Delete the dump afterwards.

UnrealGold.title: UnrealGold
UnrealGold.engine: Unreal Engine 1: Unreal Gold 226b (Manifest.ini Version=226b; Unreal plus Return to Na Pali/UPak). The game renderer is D3DDrv 226b (System\D3DDrv.dll, md5 f924e209e7bc23b90b6f0360174683d3), a DirectX 7 renderer (IDirectDraw7 plus IID_IDirect3D7). The menus are UWindow/UMenu. Unreal.ini sets Console=UPak.UPakConsole. UPak.u's import table resolves its superclass to UMenu.UnrealConsole, which extends UWindow.WindowConsole.
UnrealGold.launch_sets: CONFIRMED: the game starts fullscreen at 1920x1080x32 on all four LCD boxes. 'Play Unreal Gold.bat' calls FLEETRES.BAT, then FLEETRES.EXE -ini writes FullscreenViewportX/Y=%FR_W%/%FR_H% and StartupFullscreen=True, and sets Game/Windowed/RenderDevice to %FR_UE1DEV%. gameres.h lines 721-723 write the same three WinDrv keys at GAMESYNC time, but not the render device. At about 00:45 I ran FLEETRES.EXE -cmd (read-only) on each box. It printed FR_W=1920, FR_H=1080, FR_EDID=1, FR_GLIDE=0 and FR_UE1DEV=D3DDrv.D3DRenderDevice on .123, .145, .195 and .240; .240's EDID was present at that time. The deployed Unreal.ini already reads 1920/1080 on all four boxes. SetRes chooses the mode by searching the full DirectDraw list, not the capped GetRes list. Proof: .195's Unreal.log from 08-31 reads 'Best-match display mode: 1920x1080x32 (Error=0)', although 1080p is only the 20th 16-bpp mode on that box. .145 had never been tested at 1080p; tonight it started at 1920x1080x32 (same best-match line in Unreal.log, and a 1920x1080 frame).
UnrealGold.menu_source: The list comes from the driver and is cut short. Esc opens the UWindow desktop (UMenuRootWindow); the path is Options > Preferences > Video > Resolution. UMenuVideoClientWindow.LoadAvailableSettings copies ConsoleCommand("GetRes") word for word into a combo that cannot be typed into. The renderer's Exec runs before WinDrv's, so D3DDrv answers GetRes. It keeps each distinct WxH among the 16-bpp entries of IDirectDraw7::EnumDisplayModes, in DirectDraw's order and unsorted, and prints only the first 16 (100064f5: cmp edi,0x10). The only other filter is a max-size clamp, which is 0x7fffffff except on a 3dfx Voodoo 1 or 2. I measured the lists tonight with a probe that makes the same EnumDisplayModes call (flags 0, DDSD_CAPS/DDSCAPS_3DDEVICE). The distinct 16-bpp modes are in ascending order on every box. .123 has 15, and 1920x1080 is 15th, so it is listed. .145 has 16, and 1920x1080 is 16th, so it is listed with no margin. .195 has 20, and 1920x1080 is 20th, so it is cut and the menu stops at 1440x900. .240 has 24, and 1920x1080 is 24th, so it is cut; the menu runs from 320x200 to 1280x768. Observed in-game on .145: getres printed exactly the 16 predicted modes, ending in 1920x1080. Result: the menu lists 1920x1080 on .123 and .145, but not on .195 or .240.

UnrealGold.fix:
CONFIRMED as proposed: edit one byte of System\D3DDrv.dll at file offset 0x64f5, changing 83 FF 10 (cmp edi,16) to 83 FF 7F. After the edit, D3DDrv prints every distinct 16-bpp mode in DirectDraw's order, which is ascending on all four LCD boxes. UMenu's combo has no item limit, so the menu should show 20 entries ending at 1920x1080 on .195 and 24 entries ending at 1920x1080 on .240; these are the probe's full lists. GameRenderDevice stays D3DDrv, as README-FLEET requires. Ship it through the staged-game loop:
1. Back up the original under Games-Library\_patches and record both md5s in _patches\README.txt.
2. Publish through gvfs. The edit keeps the file size, and smbclient stamps an Oct 2007 mtime that makes GAMESYNC skip the file.
3. On every box run GAMESYNC RESET, then GAMESYNC START. The boot-time sync stays idle while gamesync.done exists.
4. DOWNLOAD the DLL from each box and compare its md5.
The survey's rejected alternatives are still worse. The 226 OpenGlDrv (verified sorted and uncapped) contradicts README-FLEET, and FR_UE1DEV would overwrite an ini-only switch anyway. OldUnreal 227 needs SSE2 and cannot join a 226 server.

UnrealGold.fix_risk: Low. D3DDrv.dll is a client renderer, not a network package, so the UCC LAN host and 226 multiplayer are unaffected. One side effect: the classic UnrealShare.UnrealVideoMenu (var string Resolutions[16]) would log 'Accessed array out of bounds' if it were opened with more than 16 modes, because UnrealScript clamps that write. That menu is not on the Esc path here, which is the UMenu console, so this is harmless. The general cautions for a same-size vendor-binary edit still apply: keep the md5s, publish through gvfs, and verify on each box.

UT2004.engine: Unreal Engine 2: UT2004 ECE build 3369 (System\Build.ini UT2004_Build_[2005-11-23_16.22]). RenderDevice=D3DDrv.D3DRenderDevice (Direct3D 8). The menus are GUI2K4 (UT2K4GUIController), with XInterface.ExtendedConsole as the console.
UT2004.launch_sets: CONFIRMED: 1920x1080 fullscreen. 'Play UT2004.bat' and 'Join fleet UT2004 server.bat' both write FullscreenViewportX/Y and StartupFullscreen into System\UT2004.ini, and gameres.h lines 730-732 write the same keys. The deployed UT2004.ini reads 1920/1080 on all four LCD boxes. The compat DB shows 1920x1080 on .123, .240 and .246 (now .195). .145 has not been tested.
UT2004.menu_source: A hardcoded table plus the current mode. The path is Settings > Display (UT2K4Tab_DetailSettings). I decoded it independently. DisplayModes[17] is 320x240, 512x384, 640x480, 800x500, 800x600, 1024x640, 1024x768, 1152x768, 1152x864, 1280x800, 1280x854, 1280x960, 1280x1024, 1600x1024, 1600x1200, 1680x1050, 1920x1200: no 1920x1080. It is not a config variable, and the co_Resolution combo has bReadOnly=True. CheckSupportedResolutions removes table entries that SUPPORTEDRESOLUTION rejects and re-adds supported ones, but never clears the list. InternalOnLoadINI inserts GetCurrentRes in sorted order through AddNewResolution. CORRECTION: the page IS persistent. UT2k4MainPage's defaults set bPersistent=True and bRestorable=True (tag bytes d3 at 0x2e369 and 0x2e36d), and UT2K4SettingsPage inherits them. When Settings is reopened, GUIController.CreateMenu reuses the same page object from PersistentStack. PushMenu calls InitComponent only when Controller==None, and GUIPage.Free() does nothing for a persistent page. So the list built at the first open (the table plus 1920x1080) survives closing and reopening, level changes, and a switch to another mode. It lacks 1920x1080 only when Settings is first opened in a session that did not start at 1080p, and neither staged launcher starts one that way.

DeusEx.engine: Unreal Engine 1: Deus Ex 1112fm (SYSTEM\MANIFEST.INI Version=1112fm). GameRenderDevice is Deus Ex's own D3DDrv (SYSTEM\D3DDRV.DLL, md5 6179c83ce1d7516908e5442ebfb4d154). The launchers do not write the render device. The UI is Deus Ex's own (DeusEx.DeusExRootWindow, extension window system).
DeusEx.launch_sets: CONFIRMED: fullscreen 1920x1080x32. 'Play Deus Ex.bat' and 'Host Deus Ex Multiplayer.bat' write FullscreenViewportX/Y and StartupFullscreen into SYSTEM\DeusEx.ini, and gameres.h lines 733-735 write the same keys. The deployed DeusEx.ini on all four LCD boxes reads 1920x1080x32 with D3DDrv. DeusEx.menu_source: The list comes from the driver and is cut short twice. The path is Settings (4th main-menu button) > Display (4th) > Resolution, which is MenuChoice_Resolution. GetScreenResolutions parses GetRes, keeping at most 16 tokens (the loop is bounded by ArrayCount of an unused Resolutions[16] local) and dropping widths under 640. GetRes comes from D3DDRV.DLL, which has the same algorithm as Unreal Gold's: 16 bpp only, unsorted, at most 16 entries (100062ce cmp edi,0x10). I measured the resulting menus with the probe. On .123, 15 entries include 1920x1080. On .145, 16 entries end in 1920x1080; the identical algorithm was confirmed in-game with Unreal Gold on that box. On .195 the menu has 16 entries, 640x480 to 1440x900. On .240 it has 12 entries, 640x400 to 1280x768. TRAP, worse than the survey said: if the current mode is not in the list, LoadSetting selects entry 0. MenuUIWindow defaults bEscapeSavesSettings=True and the Display screen inherits it, so Esc runs SaveSettings exactly as Enter and OK do. That calls SetRes on entry 0: 640x480 on .195, 640x400 on .240. Today, simply opening Display Settings and leaving with Esc drops those boxes out of 1080p.

DeusEx.fix:
CONFIRMED: two one-byte edits, and both are required.
(1) SYSTEM\D3DDRV.DLL at 0x62ce: change 83 FF 10 to 83 FF 7F.
(2) SYSTEM\DEUSEX.U at 0x4607ce: change 0x10 to 0x28.
Checks on (2): it is the only IntConstByte 16 in GetScreenResolutions. JediKnightDF2.title: JediKnightDF2
JediKnightDF2.engine: Sith engine. JK.EXE 1.01 (md5 85f8f883bbb7a167429879c899be1803) from the GOG tree with the ogg winmm.dll wrapper. DirectDraw with a DX5 Direct3D HAL path; the GUI and software renderer are 8-bit. It keeps its settings under HKLM (root 0x80000002 at 0x4011fa) in 'Software\LucasArts Entertainment Company\JediKnight\v1.0'. The XP sysmain.sdb entry for JK.EXE, which adds the EmulateCDFS and EmulateGetCommandLine shims, only matches when Jedi.EXE sits beside it. The staged tree has no Jedi.EXE, so no shims apply, and neither shim would touch display modes anyway.
JediKnightDF2.launch_sets: 640x480 8-bpp software on all four LCD boxes, confirmed statically. With no displayMode stored, 0x4146b3 calls FindClosestMode(640x480, 8 bpp), and b3DAccel defaults to off. REGREAD shows only CD Path, InstallType and Version on all four boxes. Correction: these values are not written only when Setup -> Display is closed with OK. They are saved on every clean exit: routine 0x414be0 writes displayDeviceGUID, 3DDeviceGUID, displayMode, b3DAccel and minTextureDimension, and its only caller is the program shutdown sequence (call at 0x4013c5). The boxes have no values because JK has only ever been force-killed there. .195 has UAC off (EnableLUA=0), so HKLM writes land in HKLM; VirtualStore is not involved.
JediKnightDF2.menu_source: The list comes from the driver, with a 64-slot cap. The earlier agent called .240 unknown; I measured it, and it fails there. Sequence at 0x425b60: SetCooperativeLevel 0x51 (ALLOWMODEX|EXCLUSIVE|FULLSCREEN, not DDSCL_NORMAL), then EnumDisplayModes with callback 0x426030, which keeps only 320-wide modes and tags them [ModeX]. Then SetCooperativeLevel 0x11 and EnumDisplayModes with callback 0x425e30, which keeps every mode. One counter covers both passes and they stop at 0x40. The array is copied into the device record unfiltered (0x4277e6). Setup -> Display 'Video Modes' (0x4150c0) filters only by bpp: 16 with 3D Acceleration ticked, 8 without. I reproduced that exact sequence on each box with ddenum.exe (source in evidence). .123: 47 modes, 1920x1080x16 at index 45, listed. .145: 50 modes, index 34, listed. .195 (Win7): 60 modes, index 58, listed with 4 slots spare. .240 (X800): 78 modes (6 from the 320-wide pass plus 72), and 1920x1080x16 is at index 76, past the cap. - In FLEETGL.BAT, set FR_UIARGS at the top, beside FR_ENGINE=ioquake3.x86.exe, and clear it where FR_ENGINE=quake3.exe.
- Splice %FR_UIARGS% into Play Quake III Arena.bat through a stage-fleetres.py repair() pair: 'start "" %FR_ENGINE% +set r_mode -1' becomes 'start "" %FR_ENGINE% %FR_UIARGS% +set r_mode -1'. The old string is unique to this launcher, so the pair applies once.

Quake3-TeamArena - Play Quake III Arena..fix_risk:
Low. Measured on hardware: the DLL loads on XP with a GeForce 8400GS, XP with a Radeon HD 3850, and Win7 with a Radeon HD 5450. It survives Apply at 1920x1080, and the client joins the pure fleet server without a kick.

Remaining risks:
- (a) Pure servers. They force the pak8 QVM, Apply trap included. After disconnecting, that QVM stays loaded at the main menu until the next vid_restart or map load, because CL_Disconnect only clears the flag (0x41169b). So an Apply right after a pure match still writes r_mode 3 for that session. Joining a pure server also overwrites the client's sv_pure to 1 for the rest of the session, so later local games load the QVM again. (Both are code-derived.)
- (b) vm_ui 0 leaks into a first Team Arena launch unless Team Arena passes vm_ui 2.
- (c) The flags must never reach retail quake3.exe. It would show the MB_TOPMOST 'Security Warning' DLL dialog over the fullscreen game.
- (d) The native server browser/Favorites uses the same server1..16 cvars (both modules contain 'server%d'), but nobody has exercised it on a box yet.
- (e) lan_check drift.

The 31-entry cap is not a practical risk. SDL keeps the largest mode first, and 1920x1080 was entry #1 on all four LCD boxes.
